items.title: Episode 230: DRESS — Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia
items.summary: The drug rash that is actually multi-organ failure, and the window in which recognising it changes the outcome.
items.note: Core EM structures the management section under "Resuscitate" rather than "Diagnose", which is the right instinct for a presentation that arrives looking dermatological and declares itself two weeks later as hepatitis, nephritis and eosinophilia. The episode is explicit about the thresholds that matter at the front door: start steroids early when suspicion is high and the patient is unstable, titrate fluids to dynamic measures and urine output, and refer to a burn centre for extensive erythroderma or exfoliation. It is a short listen for the walk home and the kind of zebra that is only a zebra until you have missed one.

items.title: Art of Occlusion MI: Clinical-ECG-POCUS Triptych
items.summary: Jesse McLaren's closing argument that the ECG, the story and the probe are one diagnostic act, not three.
items.note: This is the fifth and final part of McLaren's "Art of Occlusion MI" series, and the one that earns its place on the CCPU reading pile: every case asks you to hold the clinical story, the tracing and the bedside echo in the same frame before committing. Regional wall motion abnormality is used here as the tiebreaker for the hyperacute T wave or subtle reciprocal depression that STEMI criteria will not call, which is exactly the decision a registrar makes alone at 3am. Worth working through case by case with the images covered rather than reading it as prose.

items.title: EMU articles of the year 2026
items.summary: Morgenstern's year compressed into the handful of papers that should actually change a shift.
items.note: The entry to read first is OPTPRESS, where targeting a MAP of 80–85 in older patients with septic shock produced 39.3% versus 28.6% ninety-day mortality and was stopped early for harm — a rare trial where the intervention was the thing everyone assumed was kinder. Paired with it is a spinal cord injury trial where a MAP target of 65 gave the same neurologic outcomes as 85. Both point the same way: perfuse the patient, do not chase the number on the monitor, and the 65–70 target survives another year.

items.title: Mental health patients waiting up to six days in Westmead ED
items.summary: Six days boarded in an emergency department is the number that tells you where the system is actually failing.
items.note: Mental health boarding is the load that does not appear in the four-hour figures politicians quote, and Westmead's six days is the extreme end of something every Victorian ED registrar recognises from their own waiting room. It lands in the middle of a Victorian election campaign in which both parties are promising ED expansions and exit lounges — neither of which addresses a patient who has nowhere to be admitted to. Useful as the counter-argument to the beds-and-buildings framing of the next fortnight.

items.title: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) — DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria
items.summary: The authoritative running total on an outbreak that has now crossed five countries and passed five thousand deaths.
items.note: As of 3 November: 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths across 67 health zones in eight DRC provinces, with cases in five countries since the 15 May declaration. The detail worth holding onto is Kenya's nine confirmed cases and Nigeria reporting none since the last notice — that is what containment outside the epicentre looks like when it is working, and it is the shape of the briefing any Australian ED would get if a febrile returned traveller walked in. WHO continues to advise against travel or trade restrictions.

items.title: Menahan Street Band — Illusions, out 13 November
items.summary: A band already on his shelf has a fourth LP landing in three days, which is the only pre-order worth knowing about this week.
items.note: Menahan Street Band sit in the library next to Sharon Jones & the Dap-Kings and Thee Sacred Souls, and they are the house instrumental engine behind much of that sound — so a new full-length is a direct extension of a shelf he already plays. Illusions arrives on Tommy Brenneck's own Diamond West rather than Daptone, which is the quiet story here: the arranger has taken the band off the label that made them. Colemine has it listed with a 13 November street date.

items.title: Played By Humans: Jazz Is Dead's Celebration of Living Art
items.summary: Adrian Younge wants a sticker on the sleeve certifying a human played it, and has built the tool to issue one.
items.note: Jazz Is Dead's new verification platform, built with AI-detection outfit Pex, stamps any track judged more than 85% human-made — and the founders are openly aiming for it to become the next version of the explicit-lyrics sticker. The record it launches alongside is Younge and Ali Shaheed Muhammad's The Midnight Hour: Lost Tapes, cut to tape with a live rhythm section and full orchestra, which is about as pointed a demonstration as the argument could ask for. Younge's orbit is adjacent to the Daptone and Big Crown shelf, so this is both a listening tip and the clearest statement yet from that world on where it stands.

items.title: Minolta Dynax 700si review — On the button
items.summary: The cheap 90s autofocus SLR that gave every function its own button instead of burying it in a mode.
items.note: Bob Janes's argument is about interface rather than image quality: exposure compensation, metering mode and AF sensor selection each get a dedicated button, where the preceding 7xi made you cycle a single function key. That is the difference between a camera you can adjust without looking and one you fight, and it is the reason these unloved plastic bodies are worth a second look at current prices. He is honest about the costs too — a grip material that crumbles like the 7000i's, smaller dials, 3fps, and readers in the comments reporting dead top LCDs.

items.title: Introducing: The Work Shirt with Buck Mason
items.summary: A US Navy chambray work shirt in Kaihara cloth, reshaped so it still works with a jacket over it.
items.note: The pattern is drawn from old US Navy work shirts — two buttoned pockets, unlined collar — but the shoulder and collar have been redrawn to sit under tailoring, which is the specific problem with most repro workwear shirts and the reason this one is interesting rather than another reissue. Kaihara is the cloth worth noting: the same Hiroshima mill behind a lot of the denim on the Heddels side of the shelf. Only half the stock has landed, the rest is due in December, and the first release reportedly sold out within hours, so the waiting list is the realistic route in.

items.title: Eye on Ashenfall — 1.0.2 adds Earth Magic
items.summary: Today's patch adds the fourth magic element, and it is the first one built around taking hits rather than avoiding them.
items.note: Earth Magic unlocks at level 14 and plays differently to Air, Fire and Water: blunt damage that staggers, and hits that build up to three stacks of damage reduction consumed by the next blow you take — a defensive caster loop, with the effect reaching melee weapons at 60 Attack. Around it are Killer Gentoo Penguins spawning across Ashenfall with their own coin and Bramblemead shop, a fishing quest called A Reel Downer, and the X Marks the Spot trail in Umbral Sands. The notes close with a look at December's Elven Luminance update, which is where Prayer and the new building kit arrive.

items.title: GTA 6 Has Officially Gone Gold — No Last-Minute Delays
items.summary: After two delays, the build is locked and the CEO has said out loud that there will be no third.
items.note: Zelnick confirmed gold status on Monday's earnings call and then told IGN directly that the game will not move again — the first time he has committed to that rather than reaffirming a window. The PS5 date holds at 19 November, which is nine days out, and the pre-download already went live on the 10th. Still nothing at all on PC, which remains the one unanswered question on every one of these calls.

items.title: Melbourne's 12 Best New Bakeries and Cafes of 2026
items.summary: The year's openings narrowed to twelve, with a Brunswick entry that is entirely gluten-free.
items.note: The northside pick is Itera in Brunswick, a completely gluten-free bakery running five different sourdoughs — the second shop from the Kudo team, and this one takes bookings for dine-in rather than trading as a counter. This is a year-end survey rather than the monthly openings roundup, so it is the version that has had the duds filtered out of it. Spread Abbotsford to Yarraville, so most of it is a deliberate trip rather than a walk.
